newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain jails 21 Shi'ite plot suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain jails 21 Shi'ite plot suspects.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Saturday sentenced 21 people accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iranian plot to topple the government to prison terms ranging from three to seven years.
A government statement sent to Reuters said 12 other suspects were acquitted.
Six people were sentenced to seven years in jail, ten received five years and five suspects were jailed for three years.
Lawyers said earlier on Saturday that 22 people were sentenced to terms ranging from three to seven years in jail and 11 other suspects were acquitted.
The court, whose rulings cannot be appealed against, on Wednesday sentenced 15 people to prison terms ranging from three to 15 years in connection with the alleged plot.
They included two main suspects, Ali al-Mutqawi, who received 15 years jail and was fined 7,000 dinars ($18,568) and Sheikh Jassim al-Kayat, who was sentenced to 12 years and was fined 5,000 dinars.

The trial of 81 suspects -- 22 of them in absentia -- began on March 1. They were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
The suspects were divided into eight groups. Their lawyers and families attended the trial at the coast guard station in Muharraq, linked with the capital Manama by a three km (1.8 miles) causeway.
Lawyers had said the suspects could have faced the death penalty.
It was not clear what verdicts were delivered against those tried in absentia.
Bahrain last June accused Iran of an attempt to topple the island's government by force, a charge denied by Tehran.

The court, set up by the government in March last year to speed up rulings, passed the first verdicts on Wednesday which coincided with the first anniversary of the execution by firing squad of Isa Qamber for killing a policeman.
It has so far jailed about 220 people in connection with anti-government violence and protests in Bahrain, the Gulf's main financial and banking centre.

Another three suspects accused of an arson attack in which seven Bangladeshi restaurant workers were killed last year were condemned to death by the court, but the sentences have not been carried out.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the largely Sunni government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested in the unrest in the Gulf Arab state.
